c2_split: With the committed comparator admission wall (llama 223.4 ms vs hipEngine 315.8 ms at C1, worklog 20260829T215206...-1921c9) and decode 23.6 vs 25.2 ms/token, the model predicts 1.504 s vs 1.355 s = 0.90x, which is the published deficit. Contribution: about 4.8% prefill fixed cost and 5.1% decode amortization. So half of C2 is task #12 and half is projection dispatch admission.
finding: Decode cost per token falls sub-linearly with width - 1.52x off the weight-bound ideal at C2, 1.62x at C3, 2.69x at C8 - i.e. weights are not amortised across rows. The scoreboard still wins from C3 up because llama.cpp is worse there; C2 is the width where that trade stops paying.
mechanism_observed: throughput_claim_eligible is false in 80/80 AR cells of /tmp/he-c1c8-cap8, the packet behind the promoted AR row, while native_caware_decode is true in the 70 cells with width>1 and false in the ten C1 cells, which is the expected shape for a width-aware route. In hipengine/dispatch/projection.py that flag is only true on path benchmark_accepted_caware_projection; rows==1 takes row_gemv_c1 and rows>1 falls back to row_gemv_until_caware_benchmark when no benchmark-accepted c-aware projection candidate applies. The only accepted-evidence artifacts in the tree are July PARO safetensors runs (2026-07-09-...native-decode...-selected-full-rowchunks.json and siblings); nothing accepts a c-aware projection for the GGUF Q4_K_M path on gfx1100.
method: wall = width*24/rate from the published rows; per-token decode = (wall - F)/(width*24) with F = 295 ms, the measured median-of-3 wall of one ~42-token prefill. C1 landing at 1.00x the weight-read ideal (16 GB at ~460 GB/s) is a coincidence check on F, not a fit.
question: AR C2 is the one scoreboard deficit prefill cannot explain (0.90x at C2 while C3 is 1.47x). Where does it come from?
untested_inference: That admitting a c-aware projection candidate at rows>1 would move decode toward the weight-bound ideal. The bound on the prize is the ratio column above (1.52x-2.69x on decode time, less the non-projection share). Not measured: the candidates are supplied by the caller and were not exercised here.
what_this_does_not_say: The flag does not invalidate the published AR row: the walls are real and reproduce across independent runs to 0.13%. It says the engine did not use its fastest known projection route at width>1 because that route has no accepted benchmark for this model, so the row understates achievable decode rather than overstating it.
